Jira: QXR-314 (parent ticket)

↗ Open this page in the dev app

Where: Memberships > Add membership > Online > Charge card (Stripe webhooks) · Finance > Payments · invoice detail Payment breakdown

Reproducibility: 1/3

What was done (click trail):

  1. 1Open Memberships > Add Membership as an admin Pick the athlete, plan 'riz invite test 45', lane Online, press 'Pay $45.00 online', then 'Charge card' On Stripe pay with test card 4242 4242 4242 4242 Wait for 'Payment confirmed' on the reopened panel Open Finance > Payments and the athlete's Payments tab > the new invoice

Expected: One succeeded payment row and one receipt for the one Stripe charge, linked to the invoice, carrying the card details and the Admin-assisted operator stamp.

Actual: Two SUCCEEDED $45 rows 300 ms apart: payment 225 'Credit pack purchase: riz invite test 45' (payment intent + card 4242, operator stamp, no invoice, RCP-AC1-000102) and payment 226 'Payment for invoice TGWM2TD3-0001' (invoice 393, no payment intent, no card, no operator, RCP-AC1-000103). Finance > Payments lists both receipts at $45; the invoice detail shows 'Payment method unavailable' with no Admin-assisted marker. Invoice amount_paid stays $45 and credits granted once (45). During that checkout POST /checkout/sessions/{id}/sync answered 503 ten times over 45 s before 200, so 'Payment confirmed' took 54 s. The next two identical checkouts recorded one row each.

Jira: QXR-415 (parent ticket)

↗ Open this page in the dev app

Where: Memberships directory > Row actions > Freeze; POST /api/billing/memberships/{id}/freeze

Reproducibility: 2/2

What was done (click trail):

  1. 1As ADMIN send POST /api/billing/checkout/link-requests {membershipPlanId: 56, athleteProfileId: 237, idempotencyKey: <new>} and open the returned checkoutUrl
  2. 2Pay with test card 4242 4242 4242 4242 and wait until the new membership is Active (about 2 s)
  3. 3Within 5 seconds, freeze it: POST /api/billing/memberships/<id>/freeze {"resumesAt": <now + 14 days>, "paidFreeze": false, "reason": "…"} (or Row actions > Freeze)
  4. 4Wait 20 s; read membership.membership_status_transition and billing.processed_webhook_event for the subscription id from the checkout.session.completed event.

Expected: The Stripe subscription is paused (a customer.subscription.updated event with pause_collection arrives) and the freeze transition is driven by the subscription, exactly as for a freeze made later. Oracle: QXR-415-F04 family (cancel later than purchase reaches Stripe: 280/281 actor_id sub_…, customer.subscription.deleted); MembershipBillingService freeze path.

Actual: 294 (plan 56) and 295 (plan 54): POST /freeze → 200 with an empty body; membership FROZEN via SYSTEM ADMIN_FROZE with actor_id "offline:294" / "offline:295"; no customer.subscription.* webhook for sub_1UQpse… / sub_1UQptl… in the next 3–4 minutes. A later admin cancel of the same memberships reached Stripe (customer.subscription.deleted), so the subscriptions were live and unpaused while the memberships showed Frozen.

Arlo dev pass

↗ Open this page in the dev app

What was done (click trail):

  1. 1Open Memberships directory.
  2. 2Click the row-actions menu on any Active membership row (tested QA_AP rows and existing rows).

Expected: Freeze enabled for Active memberships; Cancel enabled with a confirmation dialog.

Actual: Both “Freeze” and “Cancel membership” are greyed out/disabled on every row. The Frozen tab count is 0, suggesting freeze has never worked on dev. Because of this, freeze/unfreeze toast counts, cancel confirmation, and admin freeze/resume audit-trail attribution could not be tested. RE-CONFIRMED 2026-10-17 (Phase 2 sweep): Freeze/Cancel still disabled on Active, Pending, Cancelled, Expired rows and on the newly created QA_AP membership.

Suggested fix: Enable Freeze for Active memberships and Cancel with confirmation; check the permission/plan-state gating that disables them.

Arlo dev pass

↗ Open this page in the dev app

What was done (click trail):

  1. 1Open any open invoice (e.g. INV-2026-000048).
  2. 2Click Record payment: Amount $104, Cash, Received on 10/15/2026 (today).
  3. 3Submit.

Expected: Today's local date is accepted.

Actual: CONFIRMED by a second independent pass (2026-10-15): recording a payment with today's date failed again with the same error; backdating to 10/14/2026 worked. Original observation: toast “Error — receivedAt is required and may never be in the future.” The server appears to compare against the UTC date (already Oct 16). Workaround: backdating to 10/14/2026 succeeded (receipt RCP-AC1-000149). Note the Add Membership offline flow accepted 10/15/2026 the same evening — validation is inconsistent across flows. Blocks same-day payment recording ~5 hrs/day (19:00–24:00 ET). RE-VERIFIED 2026-10-17 (Phase 2 sweep): future date 12/31/2027 rejected with toast "receivedAt is required and may never be in the future"; malformed 13/99/2026 rejected inline with "Enter a valid date." Nothing was committed.

Suggested fix: Validate receivedAt against the facility's local date (America/New_York), not UTC; align validation across all payment flows.

↗ Open this page in the dev app

What was done (click trail):

  1. 1Open People > Leads > New lead; fill step-1 names + email.
  2. 2Open the phone country selector, click “United States +1”.
  3. 3Interact with the phone field (fill/type).

Expected: The selected country persists.

Actual: CONFIRMED by a second independent pass (2026-10-15): the phone input auto-detects country from leading digits — 555→Brazil, 212→Morocco, 415→Switzerland — so the selector mis-fires even without manual interaction; full international format (14155550132) works around it. Original observation: the selector reverts to Brazil (+55) on nearly every interaction; entering 5550101234 formats as “+55 (50) 10123-4” with “Invalid phone number for Brazil”. It persisted once after clicking Email to blur first, then reverted again on the next fill. Workaround: select US, blur, then type-append a valid NANP number (+1 (312) 456-7890). (The validator rejecting 555 area codes and 0/1 central-office codes is expected NANP behavior.)

Suggested fix: Persist the selected country on the phone input's state; don't reset it on field interaction/blur.
No screenshot attached.

Report quality audit — is the QA team's report legit? (checked 2026-10-15)

Structure checks out. 186 retests split exactly as claimed (159 Fixed + 19 Partly fixed + 6 Still failing + 2 Blocked); 16 new bugs split 4 High / 3 Medium / 9 Low as claimed. All 202 IDs are unique. The 16 new bugs each carry Where / Environment / Preconditions / Steps / Expected / Actual / Reproducibility / Impact, and the Fixed retests state the observed retest behavior (not just "it works now").

Issues found in the report itself:

  • "10 pre-existing" is not traceable. The summary says ten findings are pre-existing, but only 2 of the 16 new-bug cards carry an explicit pre-existing note (QXR-279-F15, QXR-310-F20). The other eight cannot be identified per-card.
  • 6 of the 16 new bugs have no screenshots or raw evidence — all API-level: QXR-277-F26, QXR-307-F12, QXR-416-F10, QXR-416-F12, QXR-416-F13, QXR-311-F20. For API bugs the raw request/response is the core evidence; without it they are harder to action.
  • QXR-314-F12 (High, duplicate Stripe charge) reproduced only 1 in 3 runs but is filed as a definite bug. It should be flagged intermittent, and it is missing the Stripe payment-intent IDs needed to investigate.
  • QXR-415-F16 is missing complete Stripe subscription identifiers; QXR-416-F10 / QXR-416-F12 do not document the circuit-breaker threshold/configuration behind the 30 s 503s.
  • QXR-279-F15 is missing Preconditions (minor doc gap).
  • Apparent contradiction, resolved: QXR-280-F15 reports red "Enrolment cancelled" text on dev lead 267 (a converted lead whose enrolment was later cancelled). An independent dev-pass check found the converted-lead styling fixed — but on a plain converted lead, a different case. Both can be true; the team should confirm the exact lead state when retesting.

Note: this audit checks the report's internal consistency and documentation quality. It is not a live re-verification of all 202 items.

Feature gaps vs competitors (not bugs — capabilities Upper Hand / TeamSnap / SportsEngine have that Quixera lacks)
  • No waitlist. A full program (2/2 seats) refuses a third athlete with “This program is at capacity — no seats remain.” No waitlist roster, no auto-promotion, nothing in Settings > Notifications. The Academy Assistant confirms no waitlist feature exists.
  • No Coach role and no roles/permissions matrix. User roles are ADMIN, FACILITY_ADMIN, INSTRUCTOR only; no matrix UI in Settings and no “view as” — so least-privilege access cannot be verified.
  • No calendar sync. No iCal download or Google Calendar sync in Schedule (View settings = layout/density only). CSV/Excel booking export works correctly.
  • No payment plans / installments. Invoice actions are Download, Email, Issue credit note, Void invoice, Write off invoice only.
  • No series-level management for recurring bookings. Four weekly bookings created as a series have no series linkage — each must be edited/cancelled individually.
  • Promo codes don’t work with card checkout (“Card checkout does not support promo codes yet”) and there is no promo field in the membership flow at all.
